Sam Wu: Hey team — for my first change, should I aim for a single larger PR that updates a couple related files, or break it into multiple tiny PRs? trying to avoid too many back-and-forths in reviews.
Priya Desai: welcome Sam! fwiw we prefer small, focused PRs for onboarding. it's easier to review + faster to merge. :+1:
Alex Kim: second this. small PRs = faster CI feedback and less rework. also easier to revert if something slips.
Sam Wu: sweet — how small is "small"? like one function change or one logical change across files?
Priya Desai: one logical change. e.g., if it's a feature toggle + a migration, split toggle UI/behavior in one and migration in another. if it's just refactor, keep it limited to 1-2 files.
Mira Lopez: also consider draft PRs early so reviewers can comment on approach without blocking progress. use "Draft" or prefix title with [WIP].
Alex Kim: checklist I usually use: 1) run tests locally, 2) run pre-commit, 3) link any related tickets, 4) add brief PR description with rationale and screenshot if UI.
Sam Wu: where's the pre-commit config + style guide?
Priya Desai: CONTRIBUTING.md has links. quick ones: run `./dev/setup`, then `poetry run pre-commit run --all-files` (python), we also have `yarn lint` for frontend.
Sam Wu: nice. can you paste an example branch + PR title pattern?
Mira Lopez: we use `user/<short-desc>-<ticket>` for branches, e.g. `sam/fix-cache-timestamp-4231`. PR titles: short summary + ticket like "fix(cache): normalize timestamps (#4231)". include the ticket in the body too.
Alex Kim: and add the reviewer tag in the PR description, e.g. `@alex` or `@pri` depending on area. rotation table is in the README.
CI Bot: ci-bot: status: all checks pass for base branch main. remember to rebase onto main before merge.
Sam Wu: when should I rebase vs merge main into my branch?
Priya Desai: rebase before final push so history is clean. avoid merge commits unless you need them. `git fetch && git rebase origin/main` then force-push.
Sam Wu: any gotchas for first PR that often catch new folks?
Mira Lopez: watch for large autogenerated files (avoid committing them), run `./dev/check-format` to catch formatting, and don't forget to update changelog if it's a public API.
Alex Kim: if CI flakes, add `// flake: skip` in PR body and ping eng-sre for flakes. but try to reproduce locally first.
Sam Wu: perfect — I'll split the change into two small PRs, use draft early, run pre-commit, and tag @Priya for review. thanks! :relaxed:
Priya Desai: welcome aboard Sam! ping in #devex if you run into setup issues.
Mira Lopez: also ping me if the tests are slow, I can help with local caching.
Alex Kim: quick snippet for a typical flow:
```bash
git checkout -b sam/fix-cache-timestamp-4231
# make changes
poetry run pre-commit run --all-files
git add -A && git commit -m "fix(cache): normalize timestamps (#4231)"
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
git push -u origin sam/fix-cache-timestamp-4231
```
Sam Wu: putting this into practice now, will post the draft shortly. thanks everyone!
